elements.program: #11 App. A item 4: 'Dark matter is conjugate matter — alive, P.R.'s core conjecture: as χ particles (x-clumping, gated self-force) or, since v2.4, as conjugate monopoles localized in momentum'. §8: 'Dark matter, here, is ordinary matter's mirror-polarized cousin'. P4 (§4): 'Matter comes in x-polarized (Standard Model) and p-polarized (χ) representations'. First written statement: lab notebook #1, 'Version 0.1, September 2026'.
elements.school: Proposed, never derived. Minic 2020 (arXiv:2003.00318, posted 2020-02-29) §6.2: 'The proposal here is that the dual sector (as already indicated in the previous section) should be interpreted as the dark matter sector'; §5: 'their duals (that could be interpreted as dark matter Lagrangian L_dm)'. Berglund, Hübsch and Minić 2021 (arXiv:2010.15610, posted 2020-10-29), abstract: 'dark matter, on the other hand, comes from the degrees of freedom dual to the visible matter'. Berglund, Hübsch and Minic 2023 (arXiv:2212.06086) §6.4: 'the dual particles are conjugate to the Standard Model particles in analogy with the canonical fact that momenta p are conjugate to coordinates q'. Restated to April 2026 (2604.19418) and after the notebook (2610.19522 §3.2, 2026-10-14, a restatement: 'it is a candidate for the invisible matter sector'). Earliest public form: Belgrade talk slides, 9 Sep 2019, slide 5: 'DUAL PARTICLES → DUAL STANDARD MODEL (HIDDEN SECTOR?)' (image-only slides, read by eye by two agents; not code-checkable). All other quotations: lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Case for difference: the school's dark field is the x̃-face of the same bi-local field whose x-face is visible ('they both stem from the same bi-local function', 2212.06086 §6.4), and its own formalism says the doubling adds no degrees of freedom ('There is no overcounting here, because the action will turn out to be chiral', 2003.00318 §3) and that the metaparticle's entanglement 'prevents an interpretation as two particle species' (1812.10821 §3.1); the paper does not reconcile these with a separate dark sector (verifier's reading). Two readings alternate: the whole metaparticle as the dark quantum (a 2017 claim) or the dual partner alone. The program's χ is a separate species by postulate. On that case the two share a sentence. My verdict: E1 asks about the identification itself, and that sentence is the identification. The school states it from September 2019, as a proposal, once in nearly C1's own words. Same, as a proposal. What 'dual' means is E2, where the difference sits; the 'no overcounting' point is unresolved inside the school and is not a difference from C1.

elements.element: E2 what conjugate or dual means
elements.program: #11 §3, P2′, P4, P5: matter in the other Lagrangian polarization of one phase space (x, p); 'Only ω is rigid (symplectic rigidity ≡ constancy of ℏ)'; ρ: (x,p) → (p,−x), which 'the Fourier transform implements ... unitarily' (§3). No coordinate x̃ distinct from p, and no p̃.
elements.school: Three senses. (i) Foundations: x̃ is rescaled momentum, 'x≡q/a, x̃≡p/b, with ab=2πħ' (2109.12763 §2.2; same in 1606.01829 §1.1, 2407.06207 §3.2). (ii) Metastring and metaparticle, where the dark fields are built: x̃ = x_L − x_R ('In terms of the left- and right-moving 0-modes of the twenty-six dimensional bosonic string, one defines', 2407.06207 eq. 3.11); 'the canonically conjugate dual space, spanned by the difference of the left- and right-movers' (1905.09463); '[x,x̃]=iλ², ... [p,p̃]=0 . (Also, [x,p]=iħ=[x̃,p̃] .)' (2407.06207 §3.3); 'the classical motion would apparently be that of a particle in a doubled space-time' (1812.10821 §2). The dark fields are shifts of p̃: 'If we turn on backgrounds p→p+φ and p̃→p̃+φ̃. Thus we have “dark matter” fields' (2407.06207 §3.3); Minic 2020 §5 eq. 45, '(p̃+Ã(x,x̃))', with (x, x̃) as configuration variables; even in the foundations-style section, 'The dual momenta p and p̃ (to x and x̃ respectively) lead, via the canonical minimal-coupling prescription, not only to the usual fields φ but also to their duals φ̃' (2109.12763 §2.2). (iii) Field space: the fields' 'canonical conjugateness' 'is induced from the domain-space canonical commutation relation between x and x̃' (2212.06086 §6.4). The authors read the doubled side as momentum: 'Y can be thought of as a momentum coordinate' (1502.08005 §2); the length-and-radius reading 'is deeply misleading' (§7.1); 'the dual (momentum-like) spacetime' (2307.16712 §4.1); the x̃ ≡ p/ε description 'will appear in what follows in the metastring formulation' (2407.06207 §3.2). All lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Case for difference: every dark-matter statement uses a doubled phase space in which x̃ has a momentum p̃ of its own and [x, x̃] is set by a length λ (string, Planck or 'contextual'), and the dark fields are shifts of p̃. My inference: a rescaled momentum of x cannot have its own conjugate in one phase space, so even the passage that sets x̃ ≡ p/b builds the dual fields from the doubling. The record's support for 'the momentum side', BHM 2021's 'canonically conjugate dual space', names the winding space (1905.09463). FKLM themselves say (p, p̃) 'might resemble a doubling of momentum space' (2104.00802). My verdict: partial. The school means its dual to be the momentum side and says so, and on the reduced (x, x̃) space x̃/2πλ² 'plays the role of the variable conjugate to x' (1706.03305 §4.2). But the construction that carries the identification is a doubled phase space at λ², not one phase space at ℏ, and the ordinary p stays a separate variable.

elements.program: #11 P4: x-polarized (Standard Model) and p-polarized (χ) representations. §12: three candidates, χ particles, an X-condensate and conjugate monopoles. §11.4 (C4): 'each electrically charged x-polarized particle having a magnetically charged p-polarized analog', in a separate-photon form (the p-sector's own gauge field) or a shared-photon form (our photon, P4 restated). §8's benchmark: m_χ ≈ 70 MeV·α̃^{2/3}(σ₀/m ÷ 30 cm²g⁻¹)^{−1/3}.
elements.school: A proposed dual for every Standard Model field: 'Thus the entire SM would have a dual SM (which we propose, describes the dark matter sector)' (2109.12763 §4); 'every Standard Model field' is doubled as φ(x,x̃) and φ̃(x,x̃) (2407.06207 §3.5); 'every Standard Model particle has a dual fuzzy counterpart' (2604.19418 §5.1); a dual photon correlated with ours, 'distinct from the dark photon of effective field theory' (2010.15610 §5); a dual Z, dual QCD, dual neutrino, dual Higgs, dual axion. No dual charges. The duals rest on a gauging the authors flag: 'There is a possible ambiguity in this gauging which depends on which configuration variables one decides to work with' (2003.00318 §5). Heterotic placements differ: dark duals of each E8 'valued in the same E8 algebra' (2212.06086 §6.6) against 'its dual Standard Model of the dark sector, coming from the other' E8 (2307.16712 §4.3). lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Case for difference: the program's dark-matter candidates are not a dual Standard Model. χ is one benchmark species beside a condensate and monopoles; the program's one-analog-per-particle structure is C4, whose analogs carry magnetic charge, which the school's duals lack. My verdict: partial. The school's dual per field, with a photon of its own, has the outline of C4's separate-photon form without the magnetic charge; χ itself has no counterpart in the school's spectrum.

elements.program: #11 P4: 'both couple universally to H; gauge forces do not cross polarizations', taken strictly since v2.1: no kinetic mixing beyond the gravity-induced, 'ε ≲ 10⁻¹³'. §13 row 7: 'Permanent null', killed by 'Any confirmed non-gravitational DM–SM coupling'. Exception: §11.4's shared-photon form needs P4 restated.
elements.school: At zeroth order both sectors sit on one metric (2003.00318 eqs. 49–50, '(where we have included the gravitational background as non-dynamical)'), and 'to first order in the fundamental length, we can treat them as independent' (2212.06086 §6.3). Beyond that, non-gravitational terms: −(λ⁸/L¹⁰)f⟦A,Ã⟧ and scalar and fermion bilinears (2010.15610 eqs. 19–21), 'as predicted by the doubled/non-commutative set-up, and provides an explicit correlation between the dark matter sector and a visible sector' (§5); 'This correlation becomes invisible in effective field theory, and it vanishes as either λ→0 or L→∞. Note that with a particular double scaling, this term can be finite!' (§4); 'Also, the usual visible photon/dark photon coupling is subdominant to this term that is inherent in our story.' (§5); a Berry-phase-like term 'uniquely different from the usual effective field theory interaction terms between visible and dark matter particles' (2003.00318 §5); non-commuting visible and dark fields (2407.06207 §3.3). Strength unfixed: 'so here we leave them unspecified' (2212.06086 fn. 43). One paper puts the coupling above a decoupling energy: 'below which the dark and visible matter interact as required, only gravitationally', M_SM ≈ 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV (2407.06207 §5.3; 4.484×10¹⁴ GeV recomputed by two verifiers). lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Case for difference (here the record understates it): 'correlated' names couplings that BHM 2021 says dominate ordinary kinetic mixing, which P4 bounds at ε ≲ 10⁻¹³, and each is a coupling row 7 names as killing the program's candidates. My verdict: different, with two qualifications. At leading order in λ the two agree: one metric, and no cross term among the displayed terms. Hübsch and Minic 2024 §5.3 states gravity-only interaction below ~4.5×10¹⁴ GeV, the program's situation at accessible energies; but the same paper has 'the CP violating phases would come from the SM calculation and the dual SM sector' (§5.4, FOUND), and the source it cites for the term keeps the dual photon's correlation 'finite even in the limit of zero momenta (deep infrared)' (2010.15610 §5). So the school's papers disagree with one another; the program differs from all of them in admitting no coupling beyond gravity at any energy. 2202.06890's 'naturally correlated in this description' cites the modified-dark-matter papers, whose 'correlation' is the observed tie of dark to baryonic mass profiles (1709.04388 §2: 'its mass profile is tied to the baryonic mass profile'), not a coupling term.

elements.program: #11 §13 row 7: 'Permanent null (both dark-sector candidates SM-decoupled; P4 strict)'. Row 1: a knee in σ_T(v) at v* ~ 10² km/s and 'zero cluster signal (particle χ)'. #11, #1 and the literature-check note never mention Milgrom, MOND or a₀ (two agents' greps).
elements.school: Detection expected; nulls explained only conditionally; no permanent null stated. 'dark matter quanta should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter' and 'If the quanta of modified dark matter are metaparticles, this may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed' (2003.00318 §5); 'These type of correlations might be found in correlated events in the accelerators' (2010.15610 §5); 'A more concrete theory for MDM quanta will allow us to test the whole scheme of MDM at colliders' (1709.04388, conclusion); 'Thus the usual detection analysis of particulate dark matter should be revisited' (2212.06086 fn. 32); the acceleration scale offered as evidence: 'such observed acceleration scale is evidence for' the correlation (2604.19418 §5.1, on 'the so-called Milgrom’s scaling'). lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Case for difference and verdict agree: the program predicts no non-gravitational signal and no a₀ tie to baryons; the school predicts signals and cites the a₀ scaling as evidence. This is where observation could separate them, the open question in root CLAUDE.md: a confirmed non-gravitational dark–visible coupling would kill the program's candidates (row 7) and is what BHM 2021 expects. Caveats: Hübsch and Minic 2024 §5.3's gravity-only regime implies no signal at accessible energies, though not stated as a prediction; and the MDM authors allow the a₀ correlation to arise in gravity-only ΛCDM ('it may be possible to reconcile this result with CDM models', 1709.04388 §1, FOUND) while preferring a fundamental scale, so a₀ alone does not discriminate.

elements.program: #11 §8: 'χ propagates on g (equivalence principle; Bullet-Cluster-safe)'; P4: both couple universally to H. §7 and App. A item 10: momentum space's own gravity is a massive, reciprocity-odd spin-2 field X, whose exchange is the gate. §10: the dual Einstein term is 'an a⁻⁶ step in G_eff' (flag 49: not derived).
elements.school: Dark matter falls on the observed metric after the x̃-integration: 'In the above expression one needs to integrate over the dual space coordinates x̃ to get an effective description of visible matter, A(x), and dark matter, Ã(x), in classical x spacetime' (2407.06207 §3.4; also 2003.00318 eqs. 49–50). Newton's constant from the dual volume: 'the weakness of gravity is determined by the size of the canonically conjugate dual space' (2010.15610 §2); 'Note also that our G_N could vary by varying the volume of the dual spacetime.' (2212.06086 §6.2). A dual gravity sector R̃(x̃) that gives Λ; no massive dual graviton. FKLM's candidates: 'We now make use of the fact that the metaparticle couples to the extended metric (3)' (2104.00802). lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Case for difference: the program's dual gravity is a massive spin-2 field that mediates χ's gate; the school's is the curvature of a dual spacetime that sets Λ, with G_N from the dual volume, which the program does not claim. My verdict: partial. Both have dark matter falling on the ordinary metric universally, as visible matter does (the same), and both give the dual side a gravity of its own, of different kinds.

elements.program: #11 §8: amplitude M(k,q) = 4πα̃m_χ/(q² + m_φ²)·F(k²/μ²), 'k the incoming relative momentum', 'delivered by X-exchange between dual-stress bilinears'; σ_T(v) = σ₀F(v²/v*²), a knee at v*. App. A item 3: clumping in momentum space, P.R.'s open conjecture.
elements.school: No self-interaction law, no dependence on relative velocity or momentum overlap, no localization in x̃ or momentum (r9-sweep code over 41 papers, reproduced: 'relative velocit' 0 hits; 'self-interact' only as open questions). 'how does MDM self-interact' (1602.00055); collisionless dark matter 'whether traditional or metaparticle' (2109.12763 §6.2). The one force law is static, a potential 'which is of the Friedel form' e^{−αr}/r^β cos(γr), from unpublished work (2212.06086 fn. 31). The form proposed: 'the visible φ and invisible (dark matter) φ̃ do not commute. Therefore, one could say that dark matter is fuzzy from the point of view of classical spacetime.' (2407.06207 §3.3). Localization posed, not answered: 'It is natural to wonder about the mechanisms for localization of strings' (1812.10821 §1). lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Case for difference and verdict agree: nothing like §8's gate. The school's fuzzy form is a wave-like form, nearer §12's X-condensate than χ; its 'fuzzy' means non-commutation with visible fields, while 2405.08744 uses ordinary ultralight fuzzy dark matter with a gravity-only link to baryons.

elements.program: #11 §12: conjugate monopoles, 'magnetically charged topological solitons of the p-polarized sector, localized in momentum'. §11.4: the magnetic-mirror conjecture. App. A item 5: monopoles in conjugate space explaining non-detection.
elements.school: No magnetically charged or dyonic matter, and nothing localized in x̃ or momentum. Magnetic language only: worldsheet dyons, whose 'quantization of the dyon charges is equivalent to satisfying the diffeomorphism constraint' (1307.7080); 'the modular representation of quantum field theory introduces dual “electric” and “magnetic” variables, which are in general, non-commuting' (2003.00318 §3; same in 2109.12763 §2.2); Ẽ8 as 'i.e., the electro-magnetic dual' of E8, 'and they are physically indistinguishable' (2111.14205); 'The dual spacetime x̃ is associated with conserved dual (magnetic) charges in the same context' (2407.06207 fn. 11, gravitational corner symmetries). lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Verdict: absent. The 'magnetic' duals in quotation marks and the Langlands pairing are verbal parallels to C4 and §11.3, with no magnetic charge; the worldsheet-dyon remark is already in flag 67. Outside the school, Ran's dark state carries a momentum-space winding, topological and not magnetic.

elements.element: E9 vacuum and the choice of polarization
elements.program: #11 §3: ρ exact and spontaneously broken; 'The breaking is mandatory: [x,p] = iℏ forbids joint locality'; credits Freidel, Leigh and Minic with 'the idea that a preferred polarization breaks Born duality' and claims 'to read it as spontaneous breaking, with η as the order parameter'. P2′: only ω rigid; 'η = HJ, with the real structure J chosen spontaneously'; ρ inside a continuous U(1), the polarization a Goldstone angle needing a ρ-preserving potential. P5: 'The vacuum selects a polarization; ours is x-tilted; the mirror vacuum is equally lawful.'
elements.school: Spacetime is a choice of polarization, and the other is equally available: 'there is nothing special about the x^μ; we could have taken any linear subspace, such as x̃,p' (1812.10821 §2, 2018). In ordinary QM 'it is a fundamental property of quantum theory that this choice of polarization is immaterial' (1502.08005 §1); in quantum gravity 'a dynamical question' (§7); 'spacetime is a derived dynamical concept' (1307.7080, 2013), with the space–momentum split found 'when we look at solutions of string theory' (1405.3949 §2). 'The space U(d)/O(d) represents the choice of inequivalent lifts η that preserve the symplectic structure and the vacuum state' (1606.01829 §2). One vacuum-level breaking, of the dual Lorentz symmetry: 'The symmetry breaking happens at the level of the vacuum sector, and thus a choice of ground state fixes a value of δ', with the expansion proposed as selector, though 'In other words the dual Lorentz action is not a canonical transformation.' (2104.00802, 2021-04-01); that group 'is effectively spontaneously broken' within a sector of fixed p̃ (2212.06086 §4.3). ω, η and H all dynamical, and 'the rigidity of the quantum theory is encoded into the flatness of the polarization metric' η (1502.08005 §1). No potential, order parameter or Goldstone mode for the polarization (greps). lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Case for difference: the program's addition, an exact ω-preserving ρ broken by the vacuum, η its order parameter with a potential and a Goldstone angle, and a breaking made mandatory by [x,p] = iℏ, has no counterpart. The school's vacuum-level breaking is of a non-canonical symmetry of a doubled space; it calls the choice immaterial in ordinary QM; it holds η rather than ω rigid. My verdict: partial. Published before the program: spacetime as a polarization; the other polarization equally lawful (P5's mirror, held as a symmetry or a free choice, not as a vacuum); η dynamical, with the chiral structure (η, J) and 'generalized metric H=ηJ' (1307.7080); the space U(d)/O(d) of η choices; a vacuum-level breaking tied to which coordinate is spacetime; the word 'spontaneously' for that group. Not published: the spontaneous breaking of ρ with η as order parameter. So 'selected by the vacuum' marks no clean difference; 'spontaneously, with η as order parameter' does.

elements.program: #11 §10: τ is hilltop quintessence on the Maslov circle, V = V₀[1 + cos(τ/f)], 'strictly w ≥ −1' (w the equation of state, pressure over energy density), thawing wₐ ≈ −1.5(1 + w₀); 'a·ã = 1' from ω-rigidity; the dictionary 'Dual stiff ↦ Λ; dual Λ ↦ stiff; dual curvature ↦ negative dark radiation; dust ↦ dust'. App. A item 9 (C5): 'Their collapse is our acceleration', open, with the kept route dual stiff ↦ Λ.
elements.school: Dark energy from the dual geometry: 'dark energy is generated by the dynamical geometry of the dual spacetime' (2010.15610 abstract), a positive Λ at leading order (w = −1). Beyond it both signs of 1 + w are published: 'The equation of state parameter w_eff < −1 in this framework' (2202.05266 abstract, read via lit.py show; its text adds 'this rules out quintessence models'); 'Clearly, w(a)<-1 for all a as anticipated' and 'this model is clearly disfavored' (2503.20854 §3.3), but under an alternative UV–IR relation 'its effective equation-of-state parameter satisfies w(a)>-1' (§4). Reciprocal scale: 'relate the dual spacetime volume to the observed spacetime volume as' Ṽ ∼ V⁻¹ (1905.08269); 'the dual dimension shrinks to zero' as a → ∞ (2104.00802). No contracting dual universe drives our acceleration (greps for collapse, contraction, bounce). lit.py FOUND.
elements.note: Case for difference: the mechanisms differ. The school's dual curvature is Λ; the program's dictionary sends dual curvature to negative dark radiation and uses τ for dark energy; C5's collapse is absent. My verdict: related. Both put dark energy's origin on the dual side. One 2025 model shares row 4's sign pattern (w ≥ −1, wₐ < 0) by another mechanism, with DESI best fits at wₐ/(1 + w₀) = −3.0 to −3.8, off #11's corridor (r4-pheno's computation, reproduced by its verifier). Ṽ ∼ V⁻¹ parallels a·ã = 1 as an assumption at a string scale, not as a consequence of a rigid ω at ℏ.

propositions.reason: The identification, dark matter as the dual counterpart of visible matter in a Born-reciprocal phase-space framework, is published by the school as a proposal, never derived. It was public in Minic's talk of 9 September 2019 (slides, hedged 'HIDDEN SECTOR?'), 173 days (computed) before the first written statement, Minic 2020 (29 February 2020) §5 and §6.2, and was restated through April 2026; the October 2026 paper is a restatement, not prior art. Qualifications: (a) '2020' is right for print but not for the first public statement; (b) the published 'dual' is the doubled-phase-space x̃ at a fundamental length, with the dark fields built as shifts of x̃'s own momentum p̃, not the other polarization of one phase space at ℏ, so 'core' holds only if the meaning of 'conjugate' is not part of C1's core; (c) the Minic 2020 abstract clause the record quotes (metaparticle quanta as dark matter) is an earlier claim of 2017 (1709.04388), and §6.2 carries the identification; (d) a closed-access FLM paper (IJMPA 34, 1941004, online 15 October 2019) that Minic 2020 §7 cites for dark matter 'represented by metaparticles' is unread. Prior art changes no claim's status.

'Its core is published (Minic and coauthors, 2020)': the identification is published as a proposal, never derived; it is first in print on 29 Feb 2020 (Minic 2020 §5, §6.2) and was first made public in a talk of 9 Sep 2019. 'Core' does not say that the published 'dual' is a doubled phase space at a fundamental length, with the dark fields built as shifts of x̃'s own momentum, not the other polarization of one phase space at ℏ. 'their sector correlated with ours': this is the school's word, but in its equations it means couplings beyond gravity of unspecified strength (mixing terms; a dual photon said to dominate ordinary kinetic mixing; accelerator events; non-commuting fields). The clause does not say that, does not say that the program's sector couples by gravity alone, and omits that Hübsch and Minic 2024 has gravity alone below about 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV, so the school does not agree with itself. 'neither form was found' holds.

dissent:
1. Where my case for difference survives my own verdicts. On E2 and E4 the school's proposal differs from C1 in substance. Its dual is a coordinate of a doubled phase space, with a momentum p̃ of its own and a commutator with x at a fundamental length λ, and its dark fields are built as shifts of p̃ wherever they are built: 2003.00318 §5 eq. 45 ('(p̃+Ã(x,x̃))', with (x, x̃) as configuration variables), 2010.15610 eq. 14, 2109.12763 §2.2 and 2407.06207 §3.3, all re-read. Its sectors couple beyond gravity in most of its papers. So the record's 'The identification matches C1 in their foundations' is unsupported: the foundations papers (2013–2018) contain no dark matter ('dark' 0 hits in seven texts), and where the identification is made the doubling is used even in the section that defines x̃ as rescaled momentum. On this evidence the content judge's reading (a close variant, so partly anticipated) is as well supported as 'anticipated'. Which one holds depends on whether one phase space at ℏ belongs to C1's substance, and the summary's 'core' picks a reading without saying so; my suggested wording avoids the word.

2. Where the evidence goes against my case. Hübsch and Minic 2024 §5.3 joins the identification to gravity-only interaction below ~4.5×10¹⁴ GeV, before the program, so the record's 'not found' for the identification joined to a gravity-only sector (note §2–§3, flag 64, root CLAUDE.md, wiki) is too strong. FKLM 2021 places a breaking tied to the choice of spacetime in the vacuum sector, so 'selected by the vacuum' is not a clean difference either. The overlap beyond C1 (P5's mirror, η = HJ from 2013, U(d)/O(d), the positive compatibility form) is larger than the record states.

3. Against r2-dual-sm-verify (record point 1), and with r4-pheno-verify (record point 4): the note's 'the school, like the program, expects no standard direct-detection signal' should lose 'like the program'. The school expects detection through the entanglement and correlated accelerator events, and its MDM line plans direct-detection tests; the program requires a permanent null (row 7). The paraphrase 'no standard signal' can be defended, but 'like the program' overstates the likeness.

4. A qualification of r9-sweep-verify's statement that HM 2024 'matches the program's P4 at accessible energies'. The same paper says 'the CP violating phases would come from the SM calculation and the dual SM sector' (§5.4, re-read). By my reading that is a non-gravitational effect of the dark sector on low-energy observables. The paper also cites, for its mixing term, BHM 2021, which keeps the dual photon's correlation finite in the deep infrared. The gravity-only statement is one sentence, not the paper's whole account.
